functional_semantics.triton: y = x * rsqrt(sum(x^2)/K + eps) * w per row of the (batch*M, K) view, eps default 1e-6 (impl_triton.py 28, 36, 55).
functional_semantics.cutile: y = x * rsqrt(sum(x^2)/N + eps) * w per row with N = K passed as ConstInt, eps default 1e-6 (impl_cutile.py 37, 53, 63, 98).
functional_semantics.note: Both realise F.rms_norm(x, x.shape[-1:], weight=rms_w, eps=eps) (impl_torch.py 6); the engine passes only (x, rms_w) so eps is always 1e-6 on both sides.

stages.triton: One kernel, grid = batch*M programs, pass A sum of squares then pass B normalise-and-scale within the same program (impl_triton.py 22-36, 67).
stages.cutile: One kernel, grid = (batch*M, 1, 1), pass 1 sum of squares then pass 2 normalise-and-scale within the same CTA (impl_cutile.py 27-54, 77).
stages.note: Identical single-launch two-pass structure, one program per row, chunked loop over K on both sides.

dependencies.triton: rstd (line 28) is a program-private scalar consumed by the second loop (31-36); rows independent.
dependencies.cutile: rstd (line 37) is a CTA-private scalar consumed by the second loop (40-54); rows independent.
dependencies.note: Per-row statistic before normalisation, no global intermediate, on both sides.

reduction_scan_sort.triton: Lane-wise fp32 accumulation over chunks (var += x*x, line 27) then one tl.sum over the lanes (line 28); masked lanes add 0.0 (line 26).
reduction_scan_sort.cutile: Lane-wise fp32 accumulation over tiles (_rms + xj*xj, line 35) then one ct.sum over the lanes (line 37); ZERO padding (line 32).
reduction_scan_sort.note: Same chunk-sequential-then-tree sum structure; intra-tile order left to the compiler on both sides; divisor is the true K on both.

precision.triton: Explicit .to(tl.float32) on every load (26, 34, 35), fp32 var/rstd/multiply, implicit downcast at tl.store (36).
precision.cutile: Explicit ct.astype(..., ct.float32) on every load (29-34, 41-52), fp32 rstd/multiply, one ct.astype to x.dtype before the store (53).
precision.note: fp32 accumulation and fp32 normalise with a single final downcast on both sides; rsqrt primitive (tl.math.rsqrt vs ct.rsqrt) is a primitive choice within tolerance.

preprocessing.triton: x.reshape(batch_M, K), torch.empty_like(x), out.reshape; stride(0) passed (impl_triton.py 58-65, 72).
preprocessing.cutile: x.contiguous().reshape(batch_M, K), torch.empty_like(x), out.reshape, rms_w.contiguous() (impl_cutile.py 67-74); contiguous() is a no-op on the generator inputs.
preprocessing.note: Views plus one output allocation only, all inside run(); no cast, copy, repack or cross-call cache on either side.

intermediate_storage.triton: None in global memory; var vector and rstd live in registers (22, 28).
intermediate_storage.cutile: None in global memory; _rms tile and rstd live on chip (27, 37).
intermediate_storage.note: No scratch buffers on either side.

mutation.triton: x and rms_w read-only; fresh out each call (64).
mutation.cutile: x and rms_w read-only; fresh out each call (72); tuning launches overwrite out_2d (85), which the final launch rewrites.
mutation.note: No input mutation; idempotent; the contract forbids mutation.

hardware_dispatch.cutile: No hardware branches; allow_tma=False/latency=1 load hints are fixed mapping annotations (31, 43, 49, 54).
hardware_dispatch.note: Single code path on both sides.

fq_boundary.note: n is engine-provided: infer_problem_size('rmsnorm') returns batch*M*K (tilebench/data/tensors.py 657-662, used via core/metrics.py 61), i.e. the element count. Both timed run() bodies perform only views and one empty allocation besides the kernel, so there is no clone, zero-fill, scratch or cached prepack. The 3n model corresponds to x read twice (two sweeps) plus out written once; the (K,) weight, re-read per row, is uncounted.

review_items: bytes_expr = 3n matches a two-sweep kernel that re-reads x from memory; an implementation that keeps the row on chip moves ~2n and will report above the 3n model. Decide whether the metric stays at 3n (current, matches both references) or is changed to the minimal 2n bound. Non-blocking: the contract permits either mapping.
